outcome.technical: _locks.py: _is_zombie(pid) now returns (True|False|None, reason). HEAD ignored ps's exit code and returned False on OSError. New public liveness(pid) returns {alive, state, basis}, where state is running|gone|zombie|unverified|unknown. A present pid whose state is unreadable is state 'unverified', alive True, and its basis names the refusal. pid_alive(pid) is liveness(pid)['alive'], so its values are unchanged from HEAD in every case (unverified stays True and is never None), and the age fallback is never reached on a refusal. judge() reads liveness(); on 'unverified' it returns (True, '<basis> on this host (<host>)') before age is asked, so acquire's E_LIVE 'basis:' line names the refusal. errno import added. _parent_of is not changed: on a refusal it still returns None, which ends the ancestry walk; that walk only adds a sentence to a refusal and never decides one. tests/_harness.py: added ps_refusal() (an independent ps probe of this process, returning the refusal worded or None), state_refusal() (None where /proc/<pid>/stat exists, else ps_refusal()), with_stub_ps(fn, script) (puts a stub ps first on PATH, or with script=None makes it the only, unexecutable ps; PATH restored in finally), and recorded(fn) (runs a block against a capturing check). test__locks.py: the zombie block is now _zombie_cases(). pz0 and pz0b (the formerly unlabelled pid_alive case) skip through _harness.skip with state_refusal()'s text as evidence, and only when that independent probe reports a refusal. ap3 skips the same way. tasks.description: Phase code review of P157 (commits 0cff7a57, e7f472c1). At HEAD: (1) GATE_REPEATABLE = (passed, failed), and an empty gate has no step names, so gate_mean_ms is None and the gate always goes to the background; run-test-gate records empty-gate and exits 0 (run-test-gate.py treats passed and EMPTY_GATE as green), but the read-back turns it into unrepeatable_red - a task with no gate burns attempts as gate-red, a phase with an empty testGate stops at sign-off. (2) chosen_task_gate weighs gate_step_names (declared entries) only, while run-test-gate appends the affected suites (commands = commands + extra), so a fast declared step plus a slow affected suite runs inline and the CLI kills it. (3) the means take every row's durations, aborted and cancelled ones included, biasing a slow gate fast. (4) integrate_member and red_gate_stop take the first line holding GATE, which on a read-back is the reuse banner (gate_red_decision was fixed for this; these two were not). One reading for what a gate will run, shared with run-test-gate's own step list rather than a second derivation.

tasks.description: Phase code review of P157 (commits 09683a97, 3b05120c, 0bb2ad67). At HEAD: (1) compose_writer_prompt: when every gate entry is slow, plain is empty and the brief says 'Before you finish ... - none declared' plus 'Do not run <cmd>' - the writer verifies nothing, not even the tests it adds, and 'none declared' is false. The task's own suites (tests.add paths) are what the writer should run. (2) run-agent-session invoked_skills reads only the round's fresh stream, and writer_argv passes the same --skill flags on --resume, so round 2 says the skills were never invoked though round 1 loaded them; and an empty stream returns [] (read as none) instead of an unknown reading. (3) _impact defined_terms: a dotted string whose first segment is a config root counts as a config key, so 'ci.yml' in _config_rules.py and _panel_settings.py makes CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README and the build guide prose dependants of any task declaring either file.
